features.title: Built for the awkward part of spending time together
features.subtitle: Splitting is the easy half. Waves is designed around the other half — remembering, reconciling and actually getting paid back.

items.title: Every kind of split, none of the maths
items.body: Equal, exact amounts, shares, percentages, or one person covering someone else. Waves keeps the pennies honest — the split always adds back to the bill, to the last minor unit.
points: Equal, exact, shares and percentage splits
Split one bill between two groups of people
Comment on any expense when the memory gets fuzzy
Full edit history, so nothing quietly changes

items.title: Add an expense in a basement
items.body: Waves writes to your phone first and syncs later. The restaurant with no bars, the flight, the hill station — none of it stops the ledger. Your mirror is encrypted on the device, and signing out erases the key.
points: Everything works with the network off
Conflict-safe sync when you come back
Encrypted at rest on your device
Sign out and the local copy becomes unreadable

items.title: One trip, four currencies, zero spreadsheets
items.body: Set the rate you actually got once, and every expense on the trip converts the same way. Give the trip a budget, a photo album and a map of where the money went.
points: Set a trip rate once — per bill, per person or per trip
Trip and per-category budgets that warn before they break
Attach a place to any expense
A shared album for the trip's receipts and photos

items.title: Scan it. Say it. Done.
items.body: Point the camera at a receipt and Waves pulls the line items out. Or hold the mic and just say it — "three fifty for coffee, split with Arun" — and the expense arrives filled in, ready to check.
points: Receipt scanning that itemises the bill
Voice capture, including multiple expenses in one breath
Capture now with no group, file it later
Attach the photo, or keep it on your own device only

items.title: The part where you get paid back
items.body: Waves hands the amount straight to the payment app — UPI, PayPal, PayID, or a plain bank transfer — then holds the settlement until the other side confirms. Pay part of it. Attach the screenshot. Send a nudge that isn't awkward.
points: One tap from the balance into your payment app
Partial and per-expense settlements
Attach proof; either side can cancel or reject
Gentle reminders that do the asking for you

items.title: A private ledger nobody else can see
items.body: Not everything is a group expense. Waves keeps a personal side — your own spending, income, recurring bills, loans and budgets — that never appears in anyone else's app.
points: Solo expenses and income, kept private
Recurring bills and subscriptions
Loans you gave and loans you took
Monthly budgets with a category breakdown

how.title: Three steps. Then it gets out of the way.

steps.title: Start a group, share the link
steps.body: A trip, a flat, a dinner, or one person. Send the link or show the QR — people join without an account, and without a download if they don't want one.

steps.title: Add what you spend
steps.body: Type it, scan the receipt, or say it out loud. Waves splits it the way you asked and updates everyone's balance the moment it syncs.

steps.title: Settle, and stay friends
steps.body: Waves simplifies the web of who-owes-who down to the fewest payments, opens your payment app with the amount filled in, and marks it settled once both sides agree.

items.title: Trips
items.body: Four people, three currencies and a fortnight of receipts. One budget, one rate, one settlement at the end.

items.title: Flatmates
items.body: Rent, gas, the internet bill and the person who always buys the milk. Recurring expenses, monthly reset.

items.title: Couples
items.body: A shared ledger for what's shared, a private one for what isn't. Both live in the same app.

items.title: One-offs
items.body: Someone covered your ticket. Add them as a person — no group, no ceremony — and square it up later.

privacy.title: Your ledger is yours. We built it that way first.
privacy.body: Waves keeps the smallest amount of information it can and encrypts what it keeps. Receipt photos can stay on your own device or go to your own cloud drive — never ours — and account deletion actually deletes.

points.title: Encrypted on device
points.body: The local ledger is encrypted at rest. The key lives in your phone's keystore and never leaves it.

points.title: Your photos, your storage
points.body: Keep receipts on the device, or back them up to your own Drive, Dropbox or OneDrive.

points.title: No ads, no data selling
points.body: The free tier is free because the paid tier pays for it. Not because you are the product.

points.title: Delete means delete
points.body: One tap removes your ledger and your account — not a flag on a row we keep.

pricing.title: Free is the whole ledger, not a teaser
pricing.subtitle: Splitting, settling, offline and every currency are free and unlimited. Plus pays for the things that cost us money to run.

items.a: Yes. Groups, people, expenses, currencies, offline use and settling up are unlimited on the free tier and always will be. Plus exists for the features with a real running cost behind them — AI receipt scanning, photo storage and extra devices.

items.q: Does everyone need to install the app?
items.a: No. Share a link or a QR code and people can join and see the group in a browser. They can create an account later if they want the app — the ledger follows them.

items.q: What happens when I have no signal?
items.a: Nothing stops. Waves writes every expense to your phone first, so adding, editing and splitting all work offline. When you reconnect it syncs in the background and reconciles anything that changed while you were away.

items.q: Can Waves handle more than one currency?
items.a: Yes, from the very first expense. Amounts are stored in the currency they were spent in, and you can set the exchange rate you actually got — for one bill, for one person, or for a whole trip.
No, and that's deliberate. Waves works out who pays whom and how much, then hands that to the payment app you already use — UPI, PayPal, PayID or a bank transfer. Your money never passes through us.

items.q: What do you do with my data?
items.a: As little as possible. The ledger on your device is encrypted at rest, receipt photos can stay on your own device or your own cloud storage, and there are no ads and no data sales. Deleting your account deletes your data.
